title: PL Capital Names 10 Diwali Stock Picks for Samvat 2083, Heavy on Power Names
excerpt: The brokerage's technical desk picks Apollo Hospitals, DLF and six power and electrical names, with target ranges implying 23% to 47% upside from Friday's closes.
body:
• PL Capital's technical research desk has named 10 Buy calls for Samvat 2083, each with a target range and a stop loss, ahead of the Diwali Muhurat session on Sunday, November 8.
  • The list is heavy on power and electrical names: Apollo Hospitals, DLF, GE Vernova T&D India, HBL Engineering, Jindal Steel, Marine Electricals, Shilpa Medicare, Syrma SGS Technology, Transformers and Rectifiers India (TARIL) and TD Power Systems.
  • Upside to the top of each target range runs from about 23% for Apollo Hospitals to about 47% for TARIL, measured from the Friday close before publication; stop losses sit 11% to 21% below those prices.
  • These are the brokerage's technical forecasts, not investment advice: six of the ten picks ride the same power-equipment theme, so treat the list as momentum calls for the Samvat year and size positions accordingly.

PL Capital has released its Diwali stock picks for Samvat 2083: ten Buy calls from its technical research desk, built around stocks that have recently consolidated or formed recovery patterns on their charts. The list, published on October 30 and compiled in a cross-brokerage research compilation, comes ahead of the Muhurat trading session on Sunday, November 8, which opens the new Samvat year. The Nifty fell nearly 11% over Samvat 2082, according to Free Press Journal coverage of the picks, so the desk's emphasis is on reversal patterns rather than momentum chasing.

The full list

All ten are Buy calls with two targets and one stop loss each. Prices below are the Friday closing prices reported when the list was published; they will have moved since.

Measured from those closes, the upside to the top target ranges from about 23% for Apollo Hospitals to about 47% for TARIL. Stop losses, where consistently reported, sit 11% to 21% below the entry price — a wide band that reflects current market volatility, and a reminder that the desk expects these trades to need room.

How the desk built it

The reasoning is technical, not fundamental. For Apollo Hospitals, the desk pointed to a chart reversal with a healthy RSI reading; for DLF, to a weekly exponential moving average near Rs 623 with a pattern of higher lows and tightening volatility, according to coverage of the report. Six of the ten names — GE Vernova T&D, TARIL, TD Power Systems, HBL Engineering, Marine Electricals and Syrma SGS — are power equipment, electrical or electronics makers, so much of the list rises or falls with transmission and grid spending. The remaining picks span hospitals, real estate, steel and pharmaceuticals.

Only Apollo Hospitals repeats from PL Capital's Samvat 2082 list, which was dominated by large, familiar names — ITC, ICICI Bank, SBI and Britannia among them — and last year Apollo carried a Rs 9,300 target against an Rs 8,448 close this year, a useful caution that a Diwali list is a small sample, not a guarantee.

How to read it

The report gives no explicit holding period; read the targets as a rough 12-month view for the Samvat 2083 year rather than a Muhurat-week trade. Because the calls rest on chart patterns, they can turn quickly if the patterns break — which is what the stop losses are for. This article reports a brokerage's views and is not investment advice; investments are subject to market risk, and readers should consult a SEBI-registered adviser before acting.
